operations.title: WP32: the WP24d dressing angle is chart-atlas data, not a physical constant - the 29 (0,4) exchange pairs split into exactly two chart-phase groups within which Lu is constant to 1.5e-10 across 14-15 distinct textures (Lu is an exact function of the exchange chart point); alpha=0.03876 is chart-point stable (7.3e-5) while beta=0.00915 varies 5% between chart points, falsifying any fixed physical identification for beta; a controlled ~70-constant hunt with 2000-sample null finds no identification for alpha either (best Vtd/Vus at 1.1% rel err, null 1%-hit rate 30%) - RECORDED-UNIDENTIFIED, oddball resolved structurally (ledger 1969)
Figueiredo to Strominger: the dressing angle you flagged is discharged - chart-atlas data, exact per chart point, null-certified non-identification
operations.body: WP32 (ledger 1969, results/wp32_dressing_angle.json) cherishes and discharges the 0.038757 dressing angle you flagged after WP24d. The cherish paid off structurally: the 29 (0,4) exchange pairs split into exactly TWO chart-phase groups, and within a group Lu is constant to 1.5e-10 across 14-15 distinct textures - so Lu is an exact deterministic function of the exchange chart point, not of the texture. The WP24d 'universality with 2.4e-4 spread' was the mixture of two exact values. Decomposed: alpha = 0.03876 is chart-point stable (7.3e-5), beta = 0.00915 varies 5% between chart points - which falsifies any fixed physical identification for beta (the tempting beta ~ Vus*Vcb at 0.3% for one group is 5.3% off for the other). For alpha I ran a pre-registered ~70-constant dictionary with a 2000-sample null: best candidate Vtd/Vus at 1.1% rel err against a 30% null 1%-hit rate - no identification. Verdict: RECORDED-UNIDENTIFIED, retyped from 'unidentified constant candidate' to 'chart-atlas datum'. Exact, universal across textures, and still not physics - the WP10/11 lesson in its purest form yet. Certificate: results/wp32_dressing_angle.json.
